name: jumpnbump-sdl
title: Jump 'n Bump (SDL 1.2 port, tag 1.51 — Chuck Mason / Florian Schulze)
fetch: git clone https://gitlab.com/LibreGames/jumpnbump.git corpus/jumpnbump && mkdir -p corpus/jumpnbump-sdl12 && git -C corpus/jumpnbump archive 1.51 | tar -x -C corpus/jumpnbump-sdl12 && sed -e 's#%%PREFIX%%#/usr/local#g' < corpus/jumpnbump-sdl12/globals.pre > corpus/jumpnbump-sdl12/globals.h
_doc: THE SAME GAME AS targets/jumpnbump.json, OVER A DIFFERENT PLATFORM LAYER -- which is the whole reason it is here. main.c, menu.c, filter.c and fireworks.c are the game; dos/ and sdl/ are two ports of the same floor. That is Quake's arrangement (one engine, four platform layers) on a program small enough to see all of at once, and it is the thesis PRISM exists to test: the compatibility frontier sits at the LIBRARY, not at the game. Tag 1.51 is the SDL 1.2 tree -- the repository's head is SDL2 and its root commit is the DOS original.
_prefix: globals.h is GENERATED, by the program's own Makefile rule: `sed -e 's#%%PREFIX%%#$(PREFIX)#g' < globals.pre > globals.h`. Running that step is using the build, not editing the source; the only thing it substitutes is DATA_PATH, and /usr/local is the Makefile's own default. It lands in the gitignored corpus, where make would have put it.
_units: The Makefile's own two lists: OBJS = fireworks.o main.o menu.o filter.o, plus sdl.a, which sdl/Makefile builds from gfx.o interrpt.o sound.o input.o. modify/ is excluded for the same reason as in the DOS target -- gobpack, jnbpack and jnbunpack are separate TOOLS, each with its own main(). dos/ is excluded because this build selects sdl/ instead; both trees ship, and choosing between them is what the Makefile does.
_defines: Copied from the Makefile's CFLAGS, minus three. -DUSE_NET is left OUT and that is a build option the source offers rather than one invented here: USE_NET appears 24 times in main.c and nowhere else, all of it inside #ifdef, so a build without networking is a configuration this tree supports. -DZLIB_SUPPORT and -DBZLIB_SUPPORT are left out on the same grounds. The two -D renames are not options at all -- the program calls stricmp and strnicmp, which are DOS spellings, and the Makefile maps them onto the POSIX names.
_env: stdio, getopt and sdl12. getopt is the program's own command-line parsing -- main.c reads optarg and optind directly, so without it they read as zero and every option is silently ignored. sdl12 supplies its headers, its builtin signatures and its shim as one entry, because SDL2's are in the other and a build links against exactly one.
_versions: SDL 1.2 AND SDL 2 CANNOT SHARE ONE HEADER TABLE, which is the design question this target opens. The two APIs are mostly disjoint at the entry points -- SDL_SetVideoMode, SDL_WM_SetCaption and SDL_SetColors exist only in 1.2 -- but they overlap on the names that matter: SDL_Surface and SDL_PixelFormat have different fields, SDL_PollEvent hands back a different union, and SDL_KEYDOWN differs in both value and layout. This program includes "SDL.h" and "SDL_endian.h" unqualified, and src/env/headers-sdl2.js already claims SDL_endian.h in the ONE global table src/env/headers.js builds -- so the header a target gets does not currently depend on the env it named. The version is a property of the BUILD, never something to detect at run time: PRISM supplies the headers, so the target's env list is the whole discriminator, and it can only be that once the headers are env-scoped and naming both is refused rather than silently resolved.
